title: Construct actual mixed-width CRT row entry with complete lifecycle
body:
This construction closes the encoded entry boundary between a real mixed-width CRT row and the retained numerical consumer. It builds canonical paired streams and a sufficient unary precision guide from one sequential tape of declared padded axis records, then invokes the unchanged consumer and retires all 63 owned ports. The topology is compiled data; runtime moduli, coordinates and products are never decoded into host control.

The [uniform proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/07a135eee3a8da9392c4a1e01d4b89db05b4ac03/research/crt-mixed-row-entry/PROOF.md), [deterministic receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/07a135eee3a8da9392c4a1e01d4b89db05b4ac03/research/crt-mixed-row-entry/RESULT.json) and [exact source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/07a135eee3a8da9392c4a1e01d4b89db05b4ac03/research/crt-mixed-row-entry/SOURCES.json) define the scope. The complete kappa calculation is unchanged. Encoded upstream state, eight dirty numerical ports and the retained arithmetic contract remain premises. Physical key/ROM transport, production geometry, full E, persistent-bank history, binary arithmetic, native admission and outer recovery remain open.

The actual (5,7,11,13) caller state (1,5,0,9) reconstructs lower11 and right offsets(0,3). The output value is a whole-rotation endpoint; using it as a Beneš micro-row update is invalid. Short axes are idle at rows ell-1 and ell. An intermediate padded target still needs the literal table query.

For source extent L, selected node size n and P=1+sum of its declared widths, the complete source-operation bound is `2^20(P+2)^4 + 2^16(P+2)^2 + 128(L+P+n+1)`. The proof includes source scans, initialization, all numerical work, output consumption, cleanup and retained backing. This is an upper bound, not a speed measurement.

Validation on CPython 3.12.13, standard library only:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/crt-mixed-row-entry
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/crt-mixed-row-entry
```

Both registered warning-strict normal and optimized modes return `PASS_ACTUAL_CRT_ROW_ENTRY`: 27 actual-source cases, including a complete four-axis forward trace, two idle cases, mixed widths, padded states and six controls. Four disposable code mutations reject in both modes before receipt comparison. Committed bytes, every declared source pin's ancestry, official export integrity and both read-only Git-free export replays pass; all 19 exported files stay unchanged. The full-history wrapper was not run in this shallow checkout. No selected cold replay, production native run, Lean, Docker, independent human or proof-kernel acceptance is claimed. Hosted CI is separate.

Base is canonical main `7c472563474e60185e6ca101a17622133d047e56`, priority7, refreshed before submission. The overlap check covers live PR/Discussion bodies and relevant canonical-main notes; arbitrary historical diffs and unpublished work remain outside coverage. Only this package is added.

JoyboyBrian's [PR #5219](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5219) supplies the unchanged [Entry contract](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7c472563474e60185e6ca101a17622133d047e56/research/encoded-crt-entry-lifecycle/PROOF.md); [PR #5053](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5053) supplies the [current-coordinate numerical contract](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7c472563474e60185e6ca101a17622133d047e56/research/encoded-current-crt/PROOF.md). Hiroki KUMAZAKI supplies the [mixed-width Caller](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7c472563474e60185e6ca101a17622133d047e56/research/crt-mixed-width-caller/README.md). Cinna Davis, Tekalign, ToikY, Jose Manuel, Douglas Colkitt, John-Michael Smith and the retained source authors keep their attribution and notices. Prepared by Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in proof, implementation, review and verification. Apache-2.0.
